name: Post-mortem with action items and a lot of venting
text: Post-mortem for yesterday's outage, hope nobody lost too much sleep. Root cause was the config push at 2:14am that set the connection pool size to 5, down from 200, so the API basically choked under normal load. It took us 47 minutes to notice because our alerting was on error rate, not latency, and the latency alert threshold was set way too high at 10 seconds. Total downtime was 2 hours 8 minutes, from 2:14am to 4:22am, affecting roughly 12,000 users. We rolled back at 4:15am and the recovery was quick once we actually found the bad commit. Honestly the whole thing could have been avoided if the config change had gone through review, but it was pushed directly to prod by the deploy bot, so there's a process hole there. Action items: Dan to add a latency alert at 2 seconds by end of week, I'll write the runbook update, and we're disabling direct prod config pushes in the next sprint. We should also probably talk about on-call rotation because four people got paged and nobody was sure who owned what. Anyway, no blame here, this one's on the process not the person.
